title: Clean data, honest claims and the metrics that matter
course_title: Data Literacy: Spreadsheets, Charts and Business Metrics

say: Clean data, honest claims, and the metrics that matter.
This is the video for module 3 of Data Literacy.
Real data is rarely clean. People type quickly, two people record the same sale, a zero gets added by mistake. One wrong row can change a total or a decision.

panel.heading: Numbers must be accurate and honest
items: One wrong row can change a decision
Accurate data can still be used badly
High sales can still mean losing money

say: Data can also be accurate but used badly: exposing private details, or pushing the reader to a wrong conclusion.

say: Jos North, jos north, and Jos North with two spaces become three groups in your summary. TRIM removes extra spaces and PROPER fixes the capitals.

panel.heading: Common problems and their tools
items: Extra spaces and capitals: =PROPER(TRIM(B2))
Duplicates: a COUNTIF helper column
Blanks: =COUNTBLANK, then check receipts
Text numbers like 5k: retype as plain numbers
Typos: check =MAX and =MIN on every column

say: Use Data validation to add a dropdown, such as Cash, Transfer and POS. People pick instead of typing, so spelling stays the same. Collect reports through one shared form.

say: Ethical data work protects people. Collect only what you need, and say at the top of a survey what the answers are for.

cards.d: Counting who attended? You do not need home addresses.
Codes like P01 instead of names, no phone numbers, and no screenshots of member lists.
1 widow in Ward 3 may identify her. Combine small groups or report more broadly.

say: Replace names with codes before sharing. A screenshot posted in a large WhatsApp group can be forwarded anywhere within minutes.

say: For example, a women's group in Enugu has 120 members. The coordinator sends a Google Forms link, and 48 reply. 36 of them choose Saturday for training.

items: 48 of 120 members replied: a 40% response rate
36 of the 48 chose Saturday: 75%
Older members with basic phones were missing
Leaders collect the missing answers by phone

say: But almost no older members replied, because many use basic phones without data. This is sampling bias.
So she reports: 75% of the 48 members who replied online prefer Saturday, and we are collecting the other answers before deciding.

say: Be suspicious of these. And remember, correlation is not causation. Zobo and fan sales rise together because of hot weather, not because one causes the other.
Promises of fixed, high monthly returns are a classic Ponzi warning sign. Check registration with the Securities and Exchange Commission Nigeria before paying.

panel.heading: Misleading numbers to watch for
items: Cut-off axes that exaggerate change
Only the best months shown
Up 100% may mean from 2 to 4 orders
Averages that hide spread
Steady high returns promised: check SEC

say: High sales do not guarantee profit. Ada's figures are illustrative.

card.title: Was Ada's September profitable?
card.note: Illustrative figures. Total is net profit.

say: Revenue minus cost of goods sold is gross profit: 110,000 naira. Divide by revenue and times 100, and her gross margin is 27.5%.

card.title: Was Ada's September profitable?
card.note: Illustrative figures. Total is net profit.

say: After 20,000 naira of running costs, her net profit is 90,000, a net margin of 22.5%.
If her supplier raises prices and she does not adjust, she will see it first in a falling gross margin.

card.title: Was Ada's September profitable?

say: Break-even is where you cover all costs. A trader has fixed costs of 20,000 naira a month. Each bucket of garri leaves 500 naira, so 20,000 divided by 500 is 40 buckets.

panel.heading: How many buckets must she sell?

say: If the cost rises to 2,200, each bucket leaves only 300, and she needs about 67 buckets. That is why tracking costs matters as much as tracking sales.

panel.heading: How many buckets must she sell?

say: To remember. Clean before you count. Protect people and report honestly. And track 3 to 5 key numbers every week, including margin, not only sales.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Check totals, blanks, duplicates and extremes
Anonymise, and ask who could not respond
Correlation is a clue, not proof
Gross margin = gross profit ÷ revenue × 100
Track 3 to 5 KPIs weekly against targets
